tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the food at the canteen?

options.A: It is absurdly expensive.
options.B: It is appropriately priced.
options.C: It brings shame on the university.
options.D: It caters to students and teachers.

questions.cn: 关于食堂的饭菜，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它贵得离谱。
optionsCn.B: 它的定价是合理的。
optionsCn.C: 它让大学蒙羞。
optionsCn.D: 它兼顾学生和老师。

questions.stem: How does the woman feel about the canteen’s sweet things or fancy delicacies?

options.A: They never really appeal to her.
options.B: They are never actually good value.
options.C: They are within students’ budgets.
options.D: They always come at a high speed.

questions.cn: 对于食堂的甜食和精致美食，女士是什么态度？

optionsCn.A: 它们对她从没什么吸引力。
optionsCn.B: 它们其实从来不划算。
optionsCn.C: 它们在学生预算之内。
optionsCn.D: 它们总是上得很快。

questions.stem: What does the man say is one of the best things about the canteen?

options.A: The food.
options.B: The space.
options.C: The speed.
options.D: The environment.

questions.cn: 男士说食堂最棒的一点是什么？

optionsCn.A: 饭菜。
optionsCn.B: 空间。
optionsCn.C: 速度。
optionsCn.D: 环境。

questions.stem: What did the canteen undergo a few years ago?

options.A: A complete refurnishing.
options.B: A ruinous burning down.
options.C: A substantial expansion.
options.D: A massive renovation.

questions.cn: 几年前食堂经历了什么？

optionsCn.A: 彻底换新家具。
optionsCn.B: 被烧毁。
optionsCn.C: 大规模扩建。
optionsCn.D: 大规模翻新。

lines.t: I must say I love our canteen.
lines.cn: 我得说我很喜欢咱们的食堂。

lines.t: It’s such a great meeting point.
lines.cn: 它真是个绝佳的碰面地点。

lines.t: Yeah, it really is, both for students and teachers.
lines.cn: 是啊，确实是，对学生和老师都是如此。

lines.t: Shame about the food.
lines.cn: 可惜饭菜不怎么样。

lines.t: What do you mean?
lines.cn: 你这话什么意思？

lines.t: I think the food is fine.
lines.cn: 我觉得饭菜还不错。

lines.t: I would say the food is just OK, but the prices are absurd, don’t you agree?
lines.cn: 要我说，饭菜只能算一般，但价格贵得离谱，你同意吗？

lines.t: I don’t actually.
lines.cn: 我还真不同意。

lines.t: I personally think they’re perfectly appropriate.
lines.cn: 我个人认为定价完全合理。

lines.t: If it’s overpriced, why does it get so frantically busy at lunchtimes?
lines.cn: 要是真贵得离谱，那为什么午餐时间还是挤得水泄不通？

lines.t: Hmm.
lines.cn: 嗯。

lines.t: You make a good point.
lines.cn: 你说得有道理。

lines.t: I guess a lot of it is good value.
lines.cn: 我想很多东西其实挺划算的。

lines.t: Maybe even most of it.
lines.cn: 也许大部分都是。

lines.t: However, don’t you think six bucks for a slice of apple crumble is beyond most students’ budgets?
lines.cn: 不过，你不觉得一块苹果酥要六美元超出了大多数学生的预算吗？

lines.t: Ah, yes, desserts are overpriced.
lines.cn: 啊，对，甜点确实贵。

lines.t: I’ll give you that.
lines.cn: 这点我认了。

lines.t: To be honest, I’ve forgotten about those, as I never eat them.
lines.cn: 说实话，我都忘了那些，因为我从来不买。

lines.t: I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies.
lines.cn: 我从来不怎么馋甜食，也不馋什么精致美食。

lines.t: What I always go for is their scrambled egg.
lines.cn: 我每次必点的是他们家的炒蛋。

lines.t: They have such a great variety.
lines.cn: 种类真是丰富。

lines.t: Yeah, those are good.
lines.cn: 是啊，那些挺不错。

lines.t: They also come out really fast.
lines.cn: 而且上得特别快。

lines.t: Actually, that’s one of the best things about the canteen, the speed.
lines.cn: 其实，速度快是食堂最棒的一点。

lines.t: If I fancy something more substantial than a sandwich, but I don’t have much time for lunch, the university canteen is always a good option.
lines.cn: 如果我想吃点比三明治更实在的东西，又没多少午饭时间，大学食堂总是不错的选择。

lines.t: The kitchen staff work at such a brisk pace- they really deserve to be complimented for it.
lines.cn: 厨房员工干活节奏特别快——他们真该为此受到表扬。

lines.t: Totally, and it’s such a great environment too.
lines.cn: 完全同意，而且环境也特别好。

lines.t: Like, the entire building is beautiful.
lines.cn: 比如，整栋楼都很漂亮。

lines.t: It is very nice.
lines.cn: 确实很好看。

lines.t: The massive glass windows make all the difference.
lines.cn: 那些巨大的玻璃窗起了关键作用。

lines.t: I think they’re so cool.
lines.cn: 我觉得它们太酷了。

lines.t: Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago.
lines.cn: 据说几年前他们做过一次大规模翻新。

lines.t: It cost them a pretty penny.
lines.cn: 花了不少钱。

lines.t: Yea, I’m not surprised.
lines.cn: 是啊，我一点都不意外。

lines.t: It’s a very versatile space, suitable both for eating and relaxing.
lines.cn: 这是个用途很多的空间，既能吃饭也能放松。

lines.t: And for working.
lines.cn: 还能用来学习。

lines.t: You’re right, working too.
lines.cn: 你说得对，也能学习。

lines.t: I’ve used my laptop there once or twice, and there’s always a group project or meeting going on at the far end.
lines.cn: 我在那儿用过一两次笔记本电脑，最里面总有人在开小组项目会或者碰头。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: According to the woman, what view about today’s young people is not really justified?

options.A: They have a poor work ethic.
options.B: They don’t get along with managers.
options.C: They are struggling in the workplace.
options.D: They aren’t as varied as their predecessors.

questions.cn: 根据女士，关于当今年轻人的哪种看法其实站不住脚？

optionsCn.A: 他们缺乏职业道德。
optionsCn.B: 他们与管理者相处不来。
optionsCn.C: 他们在职场中挣扎。
optionsCn.D: 他们不如前辈那样多元。

questions.stem: What does the man say is important for managers to get along better with young workers?

options.A: Learning about the way they adhere to their own values.
options.B: Recognizing how they try to strike a work-life balance.
options.C: Knowing how they struggle to connect with managers.
options.D: Understanding the way they seek career advancement.

questions.cn: 男士说，管理者要和年轻员工更好地相处，什么很重要？

optionsCn.A: 了解他们坚守自身价值观的方式。
optionsCn.B: 认清他们如何努力平衡工作与生活。
optionsCn.C: 了解他们与管理者建立联系有多难。
optionsCn.D: 理解他们寻求职业晋升的方式。

questions.stem: How do young people measure their productivity levels according to the man?

options.A: In terms of the number of hours spent.
options.B: By the amount of work they perform.
options.C: In terms of the work done in 8 hours.
options.D: By the quality of the work they do.

questions.cn: 根据男士，年轻人如何衡量自己的工作效率？

optionsCn.A: 以投入的小时数来衡量。
optionsCn.B: 以他们完成的工作量来衡量。
optionsCn.C: 以 8 小时内完成的工作来衡量。
optionsCn.D: 以他们所做工作的质量来衡量。

questions.stem: What companies does the man think would appeal to young workers?

options.A: Those whose culture facilitates their advancement.
options.B: Those allowing them to do projects of their choice.
options.C: Those whose values align with their own.
options.D: Those refraining from discrediting their perspectives.

questions.cn: 男士认为什么样的公司会吸引年轻员工？

optionsCn.A: 那些文化有助于他们晋升的公司。
optionsCn.B: 那些允许他们做自己选择的项目的公司。
optionsCn.C: 那些价值观与他们一致的公司。
optionsCn.D: 那些不否定他们观点的公司。

lines.t: Hi, Tony.
lines.cn: 你好，托尼。

lines.t: Today we’re talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work.
lines.cn: 今天我们要谈的是管理者如何与职场中的年轻人更好地相处。

lines.t: We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic.
lines.cn: 我们常听到有人说，如今的年轻人缺乏职业道德。

lines.t: That’s not really justified though, is it?
lines.cn: 但这种说法其实站不住脚，对吧？

lines.t: Not really.
lines.cn: 确实站不住脚。

lines.t: In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
lines.cn: 事实上，这个年龄段的年轻人和任何一代人一样，形形色色、丰富多元。

lines.t: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
lines.cn: 是啊，但如果你在工作中很难和年轻人合作，你能做些什么？

lines.t: Well, it’s essential to connect with them, to learn about their values.
lines.cn: 嗯，和他们建立联系、了解他们的价值观，这一点至关重要。

lines.t: It’s also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
lines.cn: 认清年轻人希望如何平衡工作与个人生活，也同样重要。

lines.t: So, they generally don’t want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
lines.cn: 也就是说，他们通常不愿为了职业晋升而推迟幸福？

lines.t: Absolutely.
lines.cn: 正是如此。

lines.t: They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives.
lines.cn: 他们不愿为了工作牺牲个人生活。

lines.t: And this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
lines.cn: 这让人把这种态度等同于不愿意努力工作。

lines.t: Right, but that couldn’t be further from the truth, could it?
lines.cn: 对，但这跟事实相去甚远，不是吗？

lines.t: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours.
lines.cn: 年轻人在规定的工作时间内会拼命工作。

lines.t: But they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights, free from work.
lines.cn: 但他们希望休息时间——比如周末和晚上——不受工作打扰。

lines.t: So, how should managers go about assessing young people’s productivity?
lines.cn: 那么，管理者应该如何评估年轻人的工作效率？

lines.t: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work—since someone can work for 8 hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company.
lines.cn: 一般来说，年轻人认为自己的效率不该以工作时长来衡量——因为有人上了 8 小时班，却没为公司做成什么要紧事。

lines.t: Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
lines.cn: 相反，年轻人以自己完成工作的质量来衡量效率水平。

lines.t: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine.
lines.cn: 但我们常听说，年轻人希望的不只是成为一台大机器上的一颗螺丝钉。

lines.t: Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can’t it?
lines.cn: 这种观点很难被否定，对吧？

lines.t: It’s important to legitimize their work.
lines.cn: 让他们所做的工作得到认可，这一点很重要。

lines.t: Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large.
lines.cn: 年轻员工想做的，是对自己、对公司、乃至对世界有意义的项目。

lines.t: They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
lines.cn: 他们需要感到，值得留在一家价值观与自己一致的公司工作。

lines.t: Thanks for your advice.
lines.cn: 谢谢你的建议。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does a new study suggest about restaurants including vegetarian sections on their menus?

options.A: They may unconsciously help customers choose greener dishes.
options.B: They may unintentionally encourage customers to eat meat.
options.C: They raise customers’ environmental awareness.
options.D: They enable customers to eat in a healthy way.

questions.cn: 一项新研究就“餐厅在菜单上设置素食栏目”显示了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们可能无意识地帮顾客选择更绿色的菜肴。
optionsCn.B: 它们可能无意中鼓励顾客吃肉。
optionsCn.C: 它们提高了顾客的环保意识。
optionsCn.D: 它们让顾客能够健康饮食。

questions.stem: How was the study carried out on 750 participants?

options.A: By inviting them to taste different kinds of food.
options.B: By observing the eating behaviour of strict vegetarians.
options.C: By comparing participants eating vegetarian food frequently with those doing so rarely.
options.D: By requiring participants to choose a meal as if they were feasting at a family gathering.

questions.cn: 这项针对 750 名参与者的研究是如何进行的？

optionsCn.A: 邀请他们品尝不同种类的食物。
optionsCn.B: 观察严格素食者的进食行为。
optionsCn.C: 比较经常吃素和很少吃素的参与者。
optionsCn.D: 要求参与者像在家庭聚餐时那样点一餐。

questions.stem: How do altered menu designs affect frequent eaters of vegetarian food?

options.A: They are less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
options.B: They find vegetarian dishes become more appealing.
options.C: They tend to consume larger portions of unhealthy food.
options.D: They are less likely to choose dishes recommended by chefs.

questions.cn: 改动的菜单设计对常吃素食的人有何影响？

optionsCn.A: 他们更不可能选择素食菜品。
optionsCn.B: 他们觉得素食菜品变得更有吸引力。
optionsCn.C: 他们往往摄入更大份的不健康食物。
optionsCn.D: 他们更不可能选择主厨推荐的菜品。

lines.t: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes.
lines.cn: 许多餐厅正试图说服顾客吃得更可持续，从对环境不友好的肉类转向更绿色的菜肴。

lines.t: Although it sounds counterintuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
lines.cn: 一项新研究显示，尽管听起来有悖直觉，但那些在菜单上专门设置素食栏目的餐厅，可能在无意中鼓励顾客吃肉。

lines.t: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study’s authors, said restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat.
lines.cn: 该研究作者之一、行为科学家琳达·培根说，餐厅可以通过鼓励顾客多选植物性食物、少吃肉，对环境产生积极影响。

lines.t: However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others.
lines.cn: 然而，我们的研究结果表明，某些菜单设计能促使一部分消费者做出亲环境的饮食选择，却可能对另一部分人产生相反效果。

lines.t: The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food, and half of whom rarely ate it.
lines.cn: 这项研究涉及 750 人，其中一半经常吃素食，一半很少吃。

lines.t: No vegetarians were included.
lines.cn: 研究中没有纳入素食者。

lines.t: They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends.
lines.cn: 他们被分到不同的菜单，要求像和朋友外出吃饭那样点一餐。

lines.t: Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters.
lines.cn: 把素食菜品单列一栏，对很少吃素的人所做的选择没有显著影响。

lines.t: But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%.
lines.cn: 但它对经常吃素的人却影响显著，使他们选素食的可能性降低了 65%。

lines.t: The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef’s recommendation or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option.
lines.cn: 研究者还发现，把某道素菜标为“主厨推荐”，或者给一道非肉类菜肴配上更吸引人的描述，会让更多很少吃素的人选择素食。

lines.t: But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
lines.cn: 但同样，这些改动的菜单设计在常吃素的人身上适得其反，使他们更不可能选素食。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences?

options.A: They have found a solution to the global problem of air pollution.
options.B: They have managed to freeze polluting particles to around -18℃.
options.C: They have been seeking a way to prevent pollutants from penetrating indoors.
options.D: They have been cooperating closely on developing a new type of air-conditioner.

questions.cn: 关于诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们找到了空气污染这一全球性问题的解决办法。
optionsCn.B: 他们成功把污染颗粒冷冻到约零下 18℃。
optionsCn.C: 他们一直在寻找阻止污染物渗入室内的办法。
optionsCn.D: 他们一直在密切合作开发一种新型空调。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about existing technologies to purify indoor air?

options.A: They can be costly and inefficient.
options.B: They are constantly being perfected.
options.C: They are by-products of health research.
options.D: They can save over 40,000 lives each year.

questions.cn: 关于现有的室内空气净化技术，我们从文章中了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们可能成本高、效率低。
optionsCn.B: 它们正不断被完善。
optionsCn.C: 它们是健康研究的副产物。
optionsCn.D: 它们每年能挽救四万多条生命。

questions.stem: What do people tend to do when outdoor air quality is poor?

options.A: They keep their windows closed.
options.B: They spend a lot more time indoors.
options.C: They make more use of air-conditioners.
options.D: They try various ways to purify indoor air.

questions.cn: 室外空气质量差时，人们往往会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 他们让窗户一直关着。
optionsCn.B: 他们待在室内的时间长得多。
optionsCn.C: 他们更多地使用空调。
optionsCn.D: 他们尝试各种方法净化室内空气。

questions.stem: What did Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences say about their study?

options.A: It shows the importance of eliminating indoor pollution.
options.B: It may change the way of future environmental research.
options.C: It demonstrates the fruitful cooperation between UK and Chinese scientists.
options.D: It may make household appliances serve an additional air cleaner function.

questions.cn: 中国科学院潘刚教授对他们的研究说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它显示了消除室内污染的重要性。
optionsCn.B: 它可能改变未来环境研究的方式。
optionsCn.C: 它展示了中英科学家之间富有成果的合作。
optionsCn.D: 它可能使家用电器增加空气净化功能。

lines.t: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors.
lines.cn: 诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院一直在设法阻止有害的室外空气污染渗入室内。

lines.t: They found that if pollution is frozen to around minus 18 degrees Celsius in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through.
lines.cn: 他们发现，如果把污染空气在冷凝管中冷冻到约零下 18 摄氏度，颗粒物就会聚在一起沉到底部，让清新洁净的空气得以通过。

lines.t: Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants.
lines.cn: 他们的方法能够去除 99% 的污染物。

lines.t: It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units, so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
lines.cn: 人们希望这项工作能为空调设备的简单改造铺平道路，使其也能净化受污染的室内空气。

lines.t: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Kolkata or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools.
lines.cn: 城市中的室外空气污染是一个全球性问题，无论是困扰加尔各答的雾霾，还是影响伦敦学校儿童健康的污浊空气。

lines.t: While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive, or produce harmful byproducts.
lines.cn: 虽然现有一些净化室内空气的技术，但它们可能效率低、成本高，或者产生有害的副产物。

lines.t: When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors, but outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer.
lines.cn: 当室外空气质量差时，人们往往更长时间待在室内，但室外污染也会导致室内污染，人依然深受其害。

lines.t: It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year.
lines.cn: 据估计，在英国，污染每年与四万多例过早死亡有关。

lines.t: Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, “We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants.
lines.cn: 中国科学院潘刚教授说：“我们在实验中已经证明，只需让受污染的空气通过一个小型冷冻室循环，就能去除大部分细颗粒物和气态污染物。

lines.t: Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions.
lines.cn: 我们的研究使得在空气质量可能极差的地区，为家用电器增加一个空气净化选项成为可能。

lines.t: By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health.”
lines.cn: 通过这种方式控制室内空气污染、改善空气质量，这项工作可能对公共健康大有裨益。”

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the well-known mirror test?

options.A: It distinguishes different species of animals.
options.B: It reflects distinct traits in animal behaviour.
options.C: It demonstrates animals’ ability to recognise themselves.
options.D: It gauges the level of intelligence of various animal species.

questions.cn: 关于著名的镜像测试，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它区分不同的动物物种。
optionsCn.B: 它反映动物行为中的不同特征。
optionsCn.C: 它证明动物识别自身的能力。
optionsCn.D: 它衡量各动物物种的智力水平。

questions.stem: What does the study by the speaker’s team show about the fish they experimented with?

options.A: It meets few of the behavioural criteria set in the mirror test.
options.B: It behaves similarly to animals capable of self-recognition.
options.C: It removes marks from itself to show self-awareness.
options.D: It matches children over 18 months in intelligence.

questions.cn: 讲话者团队的研究表明他们实验用的鱼如何？

optionsCn.A: 它几乎不符合镜像测试设定的行为标准。
optionsCn.B: 它的行为与具备自我识别能力的动物相似。
optionsCn.C: 它去除自身标记以显示自我意识。
optionsCn.D: 它的智力与 18 个月以上的幼儿相当。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the results of their research?

options.A: They have conclusively established the criteria of animal intelligence.
options.B: They have advanced the concept of self-awareness to a higher level.
options.C: They incorporate more perspectives than one.
options.D: They raise more questions than answers.

questions.cn: 关于他们研究的结果，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们确凿地确立了动物智力的标准。
optionsCn.B: 它们把自我意识的概念提升到更高层次。
optionsCn.C: 它们包含不止一种视角。
optionsCn.D: 它们带来的问题比答案更多。

lines.t: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware.
lines.cn: 我的团队最近开展的研究表明，鱼可能具有自我意识。

lines.t: A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test--this is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in the animals.
lines.cn: 某个鱼种最近通过了著名的镜像测试——这是一项证明动物具有自我识别能力的测试。

lines.t: Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds can recognise themselves in a mirror, and only these animals capable of self-recognition will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in their reflection.
lines.cn: 只有少数动物，比如人类、类人猿、海豚和某些鸟类，能在镜中认出自己；也只有这些具备自我识别能力的动物，会在注意到自己身上的标记后试图把它去掉。

lines.t: This ability suggests the level of higher intelligence and awareness.
lines.cn: 这种能力意味着较高的智力水平和意识。

lines.t: This is not shown by children until around 18 months.
lines.cn: 儿童要到大约 18 个月大时才表现出这种能力。

lines.t: Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability, but our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror.
lines.cn: 迄今为止，还没有鱼表现出这种能力，但我们的实验显示，上述这种鱼在镜中看到自己后，会用身体摩擦坚硬表面，以去掉研究人员放在它身上的标记。

lines.t: The behaviours we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviourally fulfils all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out.
lines.cn: 我们观察到的行为让人几乎不怀疑：这种鱼在行为上满足了最初设定的镜像测试的全部标准。

lines.t: The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present or when the marks were just placed on the mirror.
lines.cn: 当没有镜子，或者标记只是贴在镜子上时，我们研究中的这种鱼从未试图去掉标记。

lines.t: Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window.
lines.cn: 未做标记的鱼在与玻璃另一侧做了标记的鱼互动时，也不会试图去掉自己身上的标记。

lines.t: These results show either that fish are self-aware or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
lines.cn: 这些结果要么说明鱼具有自我意识，要么说明被视为高等智力“金标准”测试的镜像测试本身可能有缺陷。

lines.t: What is less clear is whether these behaviours should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past, these same behaviours have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals.
lines.cn: 不太清楚的是，这些行为是否应被视为鱼具有自我意识的证据——尽管过去同样的行为在那么多其他动物身上都被解读为自我意识。

lines.t: Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviours in a fish satisfy passing the test at all.
lines.cn: 取决于你的立场，你可能会拒绝接受“鱼身上的这些行为足以通过该测试”这一解读。

lines.t: But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviours they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
lines.cn: 但当它们表现出的行为与通过测试的其他物种在功能上如此相似时，你又能基于什么客观依据这样做呢？

lines.t: Results from our research raise more questions than answers.
lines.cn: 我们研究的结果带来的问题比答案更多。

lines.t: What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once?
lines.cn: 如果自我意识像洋葱一样一层层生长，而不是一下子出现，又会怎样？

lines.t: Perhaps, in order to explore self-awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test.
lines.cn: 也许，为了进一步探究自我意识，我们不该再把对镜子的反应视为决定性测试。

lines.t: Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
lines.cn: 只有拥有更丰富的自我理论和更庞大的测试组合，我们才能确定自我意识的各种不同层次，包括鱼究竟处在哪一层。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What finding from the new study might come as a huge surprise?

options.A: Small children are even more keen on screens than their elders.
options.B: Both parents and children preferred to read electronic books.
options.C: Parents differed from children in reading behavior.
options.D: Children reading electronic books learned more.

questions.cn: 新研究的哪项发现可能让人十分意外？

optionsCn.A: 小孩子比长辈更爱屏幕。
optionsCn.B: 父母和孩子都更喜欢读电子书。
optionsCn.C: 父母的阅读行为与孩子不同。
optionsCn.D: 读电子书的孩子学到的更多。

questions.stem: What do we learn about previous studies of young children reading electronic books?

options.A: They came to conflicting conclusions.
options.B: They were based on small samples.
options.C: They yielded unanticipated findings.
options.D: They were focused on younger kids.

questions.cn: 关于以往针对幼儿读电子书的研究，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们得出了相互矛盾的结论。
optionsCn.B: 它们基于小样本。
optionsCn.C: 它们产生了意料之外的发现。
optionsCn.D: 它们关注的是更小的孩子。

questions.stem: What extra features should be included in electronic books to bolster children’s learning?

options.A: Those that prove simple enough for them to comprehend.
options.B: Those that produce both audio and visual effects on them.
options.C: Those that draw their attention to the educational content.
options.D: Those that contribute to their increased interest in reading.

questions.cn: 电子书应包含什么样的额外功能以促进儿童学习？

optionsCn.A: 那些被证明足够简单、孩子能理解的功能。
optionsCn.B: 那些对孩子产生视听效果的功能。
optionsCn.C: 那些把他们的注意力引向教育内容的功能。
optionsCn.D: 那些有助于提高他们阅读兴趣的功能。

lines.t: Reading with a young child is important, but does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print?
lines.cn: 和幼儿一起阅读很重要，但读电子书还是传统纸质书，有区别吗？

lines.t: As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens, so the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise.
lines.cn: 任何家长都知道，小孩子通常都爱屏幕，所以一项新研究发现幼儿比纸质图画书更喜欢电子书，或许并不让人特别意外。

lines.t: But the following additional findings might: both parents and children behave differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books, and the children who read the electronic books learned more.
lines.cn: 但下面这些额外发现可能就会了：读电子书和纸质图画书时，父母和孩子的表现都不同，而且读电子书的孩子学到的更多。

lines.t: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print.
lines.cn: 此前针对幼儿的研究曾提出，电子书——它带有字典、描绘故事情节的图像等额外功能——可能比纸质书更有优势。

lines.t: In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books.
lines.cn: 事实上，多项研究发现，电子书对故事理解和词汇增长的帮助超出了纸质书所能提供的。

lines.t: But there’s also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and the parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
lines.cn: 但也有研究指出，孩子有时在从电子书学习时投入的心智努力较少，父母在共读这类书时谈论内容的次数也更少。

lines.t: The study we’re looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children.
lines.cn: 我们今天要看的这项研究，旨在让我们更好地了解电子书对幼儿到底有多好。

lines.t: For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents.
lines.cn: 在这项研究中，研究者拍摄了 17 至 26 个月大的幼儿与父母之一一起阅读的过程。

lines.t: Each parent and child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content.
lines.cn: 每对亲子被随机分配阅读两本教育类电子书，或两本内容相同的纸质书。

lines.t: While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
lines.cn: 纸质书由父母朗读文字，电子书则配有配音演员朗读文本的音频。

lines.t: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books, but the opposite was true for the children.
lines.cn: 研究者发现，读纸质书的父母比读电子书的父母更频繁地用手指向书页，但孩子的情况正好相反。

lines.t: Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
lines.cn: 读电子书的孩子对内容的评论也更多，学到的新词也比读纸质书的孩子多。

lines.t: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books.
lines.cn: 这种更好的学习效果被归因于孩子对电子书的投入度更高。

lines.t: It’s important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple.
lines.cn: 需要注意的是，研究中的电子书都很简单。

lines.t: While they included background music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
lines.cn: 虽然它们包含背景音乐、动画和音效，但没有其他额外功能。

lines.t: It’s also important to note that there’s research on older children finding that electronic books don’t always bolster learning.
lines.cn: 同样需要注意的是，针对较大儿童的研究发现，电子书并不总能促进学习。

lines.t: Parents and educators need to be aware extra features in electronic books may increase children’s participation with them.
lines.cn: 家长和教育工作者需要意识到，电子书中的额外功能可能会提高孩子的参与度。

lines.t: However, if these features don’t draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
lines.cn: 然而，如果这些功能不能把注意力引向教育内容，它们就可能起不到支持作用。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What should we do with the unfavorable decisions we’ve made?

options.A: Regret having wasted much time in making them.
options.B: Think how different we could have made them.
options.C: Keep ourselves from regretting them.
options.D: Live with them for the time being.

questions.cn: 对于自己做过的不明智决定，我们该怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 后悔在做出这些决定上浪费了很多时间。
optionsCn.B: 想想我们本可以做出怎样不同的决定。
optionsCn.C: 让自己不要为之后悔。
optionsCn.D: 暂时接受它们。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about every single decision we’ve ever made?

options.A: It has made us the person we are now.
options.B: It has been made with a lot of thinking.
options.C: It stems from our valuable knowledge.
options.D: It benefits us greatly one way or another.

questions.cn: 关于我们做过的每一个决定，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它把我们造就成现在的样子。
optionsCn.B: 它是经过大量思考才做出的。
optionsCn.C: 它源于我们宝贵的知识。
optionsCn.D: 它无论如何都对我们大有好处。

questions.stem: What is life full of, according to the speaker?

options.A: Challenging things to do.
options.B: Beautiful things to share.
options.C: Choices to make.
options.D: Lessons to learn.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，生活充满什么？

optionsCn.A: 需要应对的挑战。
optionsCn.B: 值得分享的美好事物。
optionsCn.C: 要做的选择。
optionsCn.D: 要学的功课。

questions.stem: What is said to be of real importance when we make poor decisions in life?

options.A: Foreseeing the possibility for regret later.
options.B: Making proper use of the lessons learned.
options.C: Perfecting the decision-making strategies.
options.D: Seeing them as obstacles to moving forward.

questions.cn: 当我们做出糟糕的决定时，据说真正重要的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 预见日后后悔的可能性。
optionsCn.B: 妥善运用所学的教训。
optionsCn.C: 完善决策策略。
optionsCn.D: 把它们看作前进的障碍。

lines.t: Let me be honest with you.
lines.cn: 让我跟你说实话。

lines.t: If you are living your life full of regret, you are wasting your time.
lines.cn: 如果你的人生充满悔恨，你就是在浪费时间。

lines.t: Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today?
lines.cn: 那些决定造就了今天的你，你何必为它们懊悔一生？

lines.t: There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we’ve made, but does that mean we should regret them?
lines.cn: 我们做过很多不明智的决定，但这就意味着我们该后悔吗？

lines.t: No.
lines.cn: 不。

lines.t: I’ve had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently.
lines.cn: 有很多时刻，我坐着回想所有我希望能换个做法的事。

lines.t: However, just because things could be different, it doesn’t necessarily mean they would be better.
lines.cn: 然而，事情本可以不同，并不一定意味着就会更好。

lines.t: You don’t have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one.
lines.cn: 你不必没完没了地回想过去的所有决定，纠结当初是否做对了。

lines.t: You can’t go back and change anything.
lines.cn: 你无法回到过去改变任何事。

lines.t: So what’s the point in worrying about it?
lines.cn: 那又何必为此烦恼？

lines.t: Every single decision you’ve ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today.
lines.cn: 你做过的每一个决定，无论好坏，都造就了今天的你。

lines.t: We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that?
lines.cn: 我们想回到过去改变自己的一部分过去，但那样又有什么好处？

lines.t: We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
lines.cn: 那我们就会失去从这些教训中获得的宝贵知识。

lines.t: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are.
lines.cn: 你做出那些选择都是有原因的，而这能说明你是什么样的人。

lines.t: So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself, because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
lines.cn: 所以面对人生中的任何决定，都毫无歉意地做你自己，因为说到底，做出那个决定的人是你。

lines.t: With less time spent focused on regrets, you will finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life.
lines.cn: 少了纠结悔恨的时间，你就终于有时间专注于生活中更重要的事。

lines.t: In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make.
lines.cn: 在任何情况下，你每做一个决定，都会作为一个人成长更多。

lines.t: Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can’t let regret stop us from moving forward.
lines.cn: 生活充满要学的功课，所以我们不能让悔恨阻碍我们前行。

lines.t: We don’t know if we’ve made the right or wrong choice until after it has already been made, so it can be easy to start regretting your decision.
lines.cn: 选择做出之前，我们并不知道自己是对是错，所以很容易开始后悔自己的决定。

lines.t: But if the decision has already been made, what’s the purpose of dwelling on it?
lines.cn: 但如果决定已经做出，纠结于它又有什么意义？

lines.t: There isn’t one.
lines.cn: 毫无意义。

lines.t: All you can do is move forward.
lines.cn: 你能做的只有向前走。

lines.t: You can’t let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice.
lines.cn: 你不能让自己坐在那里为每一个过往选择担忧。

lines.t: We aren’t all perfect.
lines.cn: 我们都不是完人。

lines.t: Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later, but that’s how life is supposed to be.
lines.cn: 无论你何时做决定，日后总有可能后悔，但生活本该如此。

lines.t: You will make poor decisions in life.
lines.cn: 你会在人生中做出糟糕的决定。

lines.t: We all do.
lines.cn: 我们都会。

lines.t: But it’s what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
lines.cn: 但真正重要的是你如何对待从中得到的教训。

lines.t: Think about every decision you’ve ever made.
lines.cn: 想想你做过的每一个决定。

lines.t: Were they always the best?
lines.cn: 它们总是最好的吗？

lines.t: Of course not.
lines.cn: 当然不是。

lines.t: But look at how far you’ve come since then.
lines.cn: 但看看从那以后你走了多远。
